items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Eddie Heywood was at his height and playing in a club near the hotel we were in.

ctx.x: Benny Waters, the tenor sax man that I had worked with in Charlie Johnson Small's Paradise orchestra, was leading a quartet in a cabaret that was strictly for white, but he told me that I could come to hear him, but I would have to sit on the bandstand. I had not seen Benny for years and was surprised to see him so far away from the Apple. I went to see him between one of our sets one night as the place where he was working was one very near the Silver Slipper which should have been called the 'Dirty Slipper!…

We finally finished in San Diego and came to Los Angeles where we stayed in a hotel on First Street and San Pedro which I was told was the Japanese quarters before the Second World War began or before the Japanese bombarded Pearl Harbor. After a few days, the hotel started jumping because some of the musicians from Eddie Heywood, Jr.'s orchestra were staying there and Buster Bailey and myself got together every day with Emmett Berry the trumpeter and Keg Purnell the drummer. Eddie Heywood was at his height and…

Buster found a place where it was possible to buy one or more sticks of gage and I did the same thing. Keg liked a taste also, so between us we had some gage and juice every day. The government narcotic agents, known as 'G' men, were very hard on marijuana in California, which made it very dangerous to be caught with it and we were really taking a chance because every door in this hotel had a ventilation opening which could not be blocked or closed up in any manner, so the smell of anything that was not natural…
